nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.8
nodes.statement: First, we have to introduce some notation. Let $U$ be the collection of points in $[0,1]^d$ not on the boundary of a subcube. For each $x\in U$ there exists a unique sequence $(C({\bf x}_1,\ldots,{\bf x}_n))_{n\geq 1}$ of cubes of the fractal process, where ${\bf x}_j\in J^d$ for all $j$, such that $\bigcap_{n\geq 1} C({\bf x}_1,\ldots,{\bf x}_n) = \{ x \}$. Therefore, we can define an invertible transformation $\phi : U \to (J^d)^{\ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}}$ by $\phi(x) = ({\bf x}_1,{\bf x}_2,\ldots)$. For each $n \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{N}}$ let $\mu_n$ be the uniform measure on $(X_n,\ensuremath{\mathcal{F}}_n)$, where $X_n= J^d$ and $\ensuremath{\mathcal{F}}_n$ is the power set of $X_n$. Let $(X,\ensuremath{\mathcal{F}},\mu)=\bigotimes_{n=1}^{\infty}(X_n,\ensuremath{\mathcal{F}}_n,\mu_n)$ be the product space. Since $\phi : (U,\ensuremath{\mathcal{B}}(U),\lambda) \to (X,\ensuremath{\mathcal{F}},\mu)$ is an invertible measure-preserving transformation, we have that $(X,\ensuremath{\mathcal{F}},\mu)$ is by definition isomorphic to $(U,\ensuremath{\mathcal{B}}(U),\lambda)$. Here $\ensuremath{\mathcal{B}}(U)$ denotes the Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Next, we define the transformation $T:U\to U$, which will play a crucial role in the rest of the proof. Define the auxiliary shift transformation $T^* : X\to X$ by $T^*(({\bf x}_1,{\bf x}_2,{\bf x}_3,\ldots)) = ({\bf x}_2,{\bf x}_3,\ldots)$, for $({\bf x}_1,{\bf x}_2,\ldots)\in X$. The transformation $T^*$ is measure preserving with respect to the measure $\mu$ and also ergodic, see for instance \cite{Wal}. Let $T := \phi^{-1} \circ T^* \circ \phi$ be the induced transformation on $U$ and note that $T$ is isomorphic to $T^*$ and hence also ergodic. Informally, $T$ sends a point $x\in U$ to the point $Tx$, in such a way that the relative position of $Tx$ in the unit cube is the same as the relative position of $x$ in its level-1 cube $C({\bf x}_1)$; see Figure \ref{fig transformation}. \begin{figure}[!ht] \begin{center} \includegraphics[width=6cm]{transformation} \caption{Illustration of the transformation $T$. Note that the relative position of $x$ in the level-1 cube is the same as the relative position of $Tx$ in the unit cube.} \end{center} \end{figure} Recall that $\omega \in \Omega$ denotes a particular realization of the fat fractal percolation process. For $x \in U$, we define the following event. \[ A^x := \left\{\omega: \text{if we set } \omega(C(\textbf{x}_1,\ldots,\textbf{x}_n)) = 1 \text{ for all } n \geq 1, \text{ then } C_{\text{fat}}^{x} \neq \{x\} \right\}. \] In other words, $A^{x}$ consists of those configurations $\omega$ such that when we change the configuration by retaining all $C(\textbf{x}_1,\ldots,\textbf{x}_n)$, then in this new configuration, $x$ is in the same connected component as some $y \neq x$. Observe that \begin{equation} A^x \cap \{ x\in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}\} =\{ x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}} \}. \end{equation} It is easy to see that $A^{x}$ is a tail event. Hence, by Kolmogorov's 0-1 law we get $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{x}) \in \{0,1\}$ for all $x\in U$. However, a priori it is not clear that for almost all $x$ in the unit cube $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)$ has the same value. To this end, define the set $V:=\{x\in U: \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{x})=0\}$. We will show that $\lambda(V)\in \{0,1\}$. Recall that the relative position of $Tx$ in the unit cube is the same as the relative position of $x$ in the level-1 cube $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$. It is possible to construct a coupling between the fractal process in the unit cube and the fractal process in $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$, given that $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$ is retained, with the following property: For every cube $C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}})$ in $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$, it is the case that if $TC(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}})$ is retained in the fractal process in the unit cube, then $C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}})$ is also retained in the fractal process in $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$, given that $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$ is retained. It is straightforward that such a coupling exists since the retention probabilities $p_n$ are non-decreasing in $n$. Hence, \begin{equation} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{Tx}) \leq \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x | C(\mathbf{x}_1) \text{ is retained}). \end{equation} Furthermore, since $A^x$ is a tail event, we have \begin{equation} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)=\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x | C(\mathbf{x}_1) \text{ is retained}). \end{equation} It follows from \eqref{A^Tx ineq} and \eqref{cond eq} that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{Tx}) \leq \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)$ for all $x$. This implies that $V \subset T^{-1} V$. Because $T$ is measure preserving it follows that \[ \lambda(V \Delta T^{-1} V) = \lambda(V \setminus T^{-1}V) + \lambda(T^{-1}V \setminus V) = 0+\lambda(T^{-1}V) - \lambda(V) = 0. \] Ergodicity of $T$ now yields that $\lambda(V) \in \{0,1\}$. Suppose $\lambda(V)=0$. Then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}})=\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\{x\in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}\} \setminus A^x)=0$ for almost all $x\in [0,1]^d$, by \eqref{def A^x}. Applying Fubini's theorem gives \begin{eqnarray*} \ensuremath{\mathbb{E}} \lambda (\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}) &=& \int_{\Omega}\int_{[0,1]^{d}} 1_{\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}}(x,\omega)d\lambda d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} \\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^{d}}\int_{\Omega} 1_{\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}}(x,\omega) d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} d\lambda\\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^{d}} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}) d\lambda = 0. \end{eqnarray*} Therefore $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}})=0$ a.s. By Theorem \ref{thm12} we have $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}})> 0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction. Next suppose that $\lambda(V)=1$. Then with a similar argument we can show that $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}})=0$ and $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}})>0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction.
nodes.statement_short: Kolmogorov 0-1 law plus ergodicity of the shift $T$ give $\lambda(V)\in\{0,1\}$; Fubini then gives each alternative. The key step is the monotone coupling $P(A^{Tx})\le P(A^x)$.

nodes.name: Event A^x
nodes.statement: Recall that $\omega \in \Omega$ denotes a particular realization of the fat fractal percolation process. For $x \in U$, we define the following event. \[ A^x := \left\{\omega: \text{if we set } \omega(C(\textbf{x}_1,\ldots,\textbf{x}_n)) = 1 \text{ for all } n \geq 1, \text{ then } C_{\text{fat}}^{x} \neq \{x\} \right\}. \] In other words, $A^{x}$ consists of those configurations $\omega$ such that when we change the configuration by retaining all $C(\textbf{x}_1,\ldots,\textbf{x}_n)$, then in this new configuration, $x$ is in the same connected component as some $y \neq x$. Observe that \begin{equation} A^x \cap \{ x\in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}\} =\{ x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}} \}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define the event $A^x$ and relate it to $D^c$ via (19).

nodes.name: A^x and the connected part
nodes.statement: A^x \cap \{ x\in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}\} =\{ x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}} \}.
nodes.label: def A^x

nodes.name: 0-1 law
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that $A^{x}$ is a tail event. Hence, by Kolmogorov's 0-1 law we get $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{x}) \in \{0,1\}$ for all $x\in U$.
nodes.statement_short: Kolmogorov's 0-1 law gives $P(A^x)\in\{0,1\}$.

nodes.name: Set V
nodes.statement: However, a priori it is not clear that for almost all $x$ in the unit cube $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)$ has the same value. To this end, define the set $V:=\{x\in U: \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{x})=0\}$. We will show that $\lambda(V)\in \{0,1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $V=\{x:P(A^x)=0\}$.

nodes.name: Coupling inequality
nodes.statement: Recall that the relative position of $Tx$ in the unit cube is the same as the relative position of $x$ in the level-1 cube $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$. It is possible to construct a coupling between the fractal process in the unit cube and the fractal process in $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$, given that $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$ is retained, with the following property: For every cube $C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}})$ in $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$, it is the case that if $TC(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}})$ is retained in the fractal process in the unit cube, then $C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}})$ is also retained in the fractal process in $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$, given that $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$ is retained. It is straightforward that such a coupling exists since the retention probabilities $p_n$ are non-decreasing in $n$. Hence, \begin{equation} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{Tx}) \leq \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x | C(\mathbf{x}_1) \text{ is retained}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Monotone coupling yields (20).

nodes.name: Coupling inequality for A^{Tx}
nodes.statement: \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{Tx}) \leq \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x | C(\mathbf{x}_1) \text{ is retained}).
nodes.label: A^Tx ineq

nodes.name: Tail identity
nodes.statement: Furthermore, since $A^x$ is a tail event, we have \begin{equation} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)=\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x | C(\mathbf{x}_1) \text{ is retained}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Tail event is independent of retention of $C(\mathbf{x}_1)$.

nodes.name: Tail event conditional probability
nodes.statement: \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)=\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x | C(\mathbf{x}_1) \text{ is retained}).
nodes.label: cond eq

nodes.name: Ergodicity
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{A^Tx ineq} and \eqref{cond eq} that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^{Tx}) \leq \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)$ for all $x$. This implies that $V \subset T^{-1} V$. Because $T$ is measure preserving it follows that \[ \lambda(V \Delta T^{-1} V) = \lambda(V \setminus T^{-1}V) + \lambda(T^{-1}V \setminus V) = 0+\lambda(T^{-1}V) - \lambda(V) = 0. \] Ergodicity of $T$ now yields that $\lambda(V) \in \{0,1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Invariance of $V$ and ergodicity give $\lambda(V)\in\{0,1\}$.

nodes.name: Case lambda(V)=0
nodes.statement: Suppose $\lambda(V)=0$. Then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}})=\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\{x\in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}\} \setminus A^x)=0$ for almost all $x\in [0,1]^d$, by \eqref{def A^x}. Applying Fubini's theorem gives \begin{eqnarray*} \ensuremath{\mathbb{E}} \lambda (\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}) &=& \int_{\Omega}\int_{[0,1]^{d}} 1_{\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}}(x,\omega)d\lambda d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} \\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^{d}}\int_{\Omega} 1_{\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}}(x,\omega) d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} d\lambda\\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^{d}} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \in \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}}) d\lambda = 0. \end{eqnarray*} Therefore $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}})=0$ a.s. By Theorem \ref{thm12} we have $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}})> 0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction.
nodes.statement_short: If $\lambda(V)=0$, Fubini gives zero dust measure and Theorem 1.7 positive connected measure.

nodes.name: Case lambda(V)=1
nodes.statement: Next suppose that $\lambda(V)=1$. Then with a similar argument we can show that $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{c}})=0$ and $\lambda(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}^{d}})>0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction.
nodes.statement_short: Symmetric case $\lambda(V)=1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.9
nodes.statement_short: (i) countable union, translation invariance and FKG; (ii) Fubini over vertical lines plus Theorem 1.8; (iii) Borel-Cantelli.

nodes.name: Part (i)
nodes.statement: (i) Suppose that $\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}$ has a non-empty interior with positive probability. Then we have \begin{eqnarray*} 0 &<& \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}} \text{ has non-empty interior}) \\ &=& \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\exists n, \exists \ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n: C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n) \subset \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}) \\ &\leq& \sum_{ n, \ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n) \subset \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}). \end{eqnarray*} Since we sum over countably many cubes, there must exist $n$ and $\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n$ such that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n) \subset \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}) > 0$. Hence, by translation invariance, $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n) \subset \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}) > 0$ for this specific $n$ and all $\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n$. We can apply the FKG inequality to obtain $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}} = [0,1]^d) = \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n) \subset \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}} \,\forall \ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_1,\ldots,\ensuremath{\mathbf{i}}_n) >0$. Since $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}} = [0,1]^d) = \prod_{n=1}^{\infty} p_n^{N^{dn}}$, this proves the first part of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Non-empty interior with positive probability forces full retention with positive probability (FKG).

nodes.name: Part (ii)
nodes.statement_short: Fubini over fully retained vertical segments, then Theorem 1.8.

nodes.name: Positive measure of fully retained lines
nodes.statement: \lambda_{d-1}(\{x\in [0,1]^{d-1} : \{x\}\times [0,1] \subset \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}} \}) > 0
nodes.label: strictly positive

nodes.name: Part (iii)
nodes.statement: (iii) Next assume that $\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} p_n^{N^{dn}} > 0$. For each level $n$, we have $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}^n=\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}^{n-1}) \geq p_n^{N^{dn}}$. Since $\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} p_n^{N^{dn}} > 0$ is equivalent to $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}( 1 - p_n^{N^{dn}}) < \infty$, we have \[ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}^n\neq \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}^{n-1}) \leq \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (1 - p_n^{N^{dn}}) < \infty. \] Applying the Borel-Cantelli lemma gives that, with probability 1, $\{\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}^n \neq \ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}^{n-1}\}$ occurs for only finitely many $n$. Hence, with probability 1 there exists an $n$ such that $\ensuremath{D_{\text{fat}}}$ can be written as the union of level-$n$ cubes.
nodes.statement_short: Borel-Cantelli: only finitely many levels lose cubes.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.11
nodes.statement: $(iii) \Rightarrow (ii)$. Trivial. $(ii) \Rightarrow (i)$. Suppose $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \mbox{ connected to } y) > 0$ for all $x,y \in U$, for some set $U\subset [0,1]^2$ with $\lambda(U) > 0$. Fix $y\in U$. By Fubini's theorem \begin{eqnarray*} \ensuremath{\mathbb{E}} \lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) &=& \int_{\Omega} \int_{[0,1]^2} 1_{D^c_{\text{fat}}}(x,\omega) d\lambda(x) d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\omega) \\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^2} \int_{\Omega} 1_{D^c_{\text{fat}}}(x,\omega) d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\omega) d\lambda(x) \\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^2} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D^c_{\text{fat}}) d\lambda(x) \\ &\geq& \int_{U\setminus \{y\}} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \mbox{ connected to } y) d\lambda(x) > 0. \end{eqnarray*} Hence $\lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) > 0$ with positive probability. By Theorem \ref{thm lebesgue} it follows that $\lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) > 0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction of the fat fractal process. $(i) \Rightarrow (iii)$. Next suppose that $\lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) > 0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction of the fat fractal process. For points $x\in[0,1]^2$ not on the boundary of a subcube, define the event $A^x$ as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm lebesgue}. It follows from the proof of Theorem \ref{thm lebesgue} that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)=1$ for all $x\in V$, for some set $V\subset[0,1]^2$ with $\lambda(V)=1$. By \eqref{def A^x} we have for all $x\in V$ \[ \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D^c_{\text{fat}})= \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D_{\text{fat}})>0. \] Let $x\in V$. Then \[ 0 < \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D^c_{\text{fat}}) \leq \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\mbox{diam}(C^x_{\text{fat}}) > \textstyle{\frac{1}{n}}), \] where $\mbox{diam}(C^x_{\text{fat}})$ denotes the diameter of the set $C^x_{\text{fat}}$. So there exists a natural number $n_x$ such that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\mbox{diam}(C^x_{\text{fat}}) > \frac{1}{n_{x}}) > 0.$ Hence \[ \textstyle {\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}}(x \mbox{ connected to } S(x,\frac{1}{2n_{x}})) > 0, \] where $S(x,\frac{1}{2n_{x}})$ is a circle centered at $x$ with radius $\frac{1}{2n_{x}}$. Write $x=(x_1,x_2)$ and define the following subsets of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^2$ \begin{eqnarray*} H_1 &=& \textstyle [0,1] \times [x_2-\frac{1}{4n_x},x_2], \\ H_2 &=& \textstyle [0,1] \times [x_2,x_2+\frac{1}{4n_x}], \\ V_1 &=& \textstyle [x_1-\frac{1}{4n_x},x_1] \times [0,1], \\ V_2 &=& \textstyle [x_1,x_1+\frac{1}{4n_x}] \times [0,1]. \end{eqnarray*} Note that for every $x \in [0,1]^2$ it is the case that at least one horizontal strip $H_i$ and at least one vertical strip $V_j$ is entirely contained in $[0,1]^2$. Define the event $\Gamma_x$ by \begin{eqnarray*} \Gamma_x &=& \bigcap_{i\in\{1,2\}:H_i \subset [0,1]^2} \{ \mbox{horizontal crossing in } H_i \} \\ &\cap& \bigcap_{j\in\{1,2\}:V_j \subset [0,1]^2}\{ \mbox{vertical crossing in } V_j \}. \end{eqnarray*} See Figure \ref{fig Gamma_x} for an illustration of the event $\Gamma_x$. From Theorem 2 in \cite{ChaChaDur} it follows that in the MFP model with parameter $p \geq p_c(N,2)$, the limit set $D_p$ connects the left-hand side of $[0,1]^2$ with its right-hand side with positive probability. It then follows from the RSW lemma (e.g.\ Lemma 5.1 in \cite{DekMee}) and the FKG inequality that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{p}(\Gamma_x)>0$. Let $A_{n}$ denote the event of complete retention until level $n$, i.e.\ $\omega(C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}}))=1$ for all $\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}} \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{J}}^{(n-1)}$. Since $\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} p_n >0$ there exists an integer $n_0$ such that $p_{n} \geq p_c(N,2)$ for all $n \geq n_0$. Hence, the probability measure $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{\text{fat}}(\cdot | A_{n_0}$) dominates $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{p_{c}(N,2)}(\cdot)$. Since $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{\text{fat}}(A_{n_0})>0$ it follows that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{\text{fat}}(\Gamma_x) > 0$. \begin{figure}[!ht] \begin{center} \includegraphics[width=7cm]{Gamma_x} \caption{Realization of the event $\Gamma_x$.} \end{center} \end{figure} Observe that for $x,y \in V$ \begin{eqnarray*} \lefteqn{ \{ x \mbox{ connected to } y \} } \\ &\supset& \{ x \mbox{ connected to } S(x,\textstyle{\frac{1}{2n_x}}) \} \cap \Gamma_x \cap \{ y \mbox{ connected to } S(y,\textstyle{\frac{1}{2n_y}}) \} \cap \Gamma_y. \end{eqnarray*} Since all four events on the right-hand side are increasing and have positive probability, we can apply the FKG inequality to conclude that for all $x,y\in V$ we have $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \mbox{ connected to } y) > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Cycle of implications via Fubini and Theorem 1.8; for (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii), RSW and FKG connect any two points through crossings of thin strips.

nodes.name: (iii)=>(ii)
nodes.statement: $(iii) \Rightarrow (ii)$. Trivial.
nodes.statement_short: (iii) implies (ii) trivially.

nodes.name: (ii)=>(i)
nodes.statement: $(ii) \Rightarrow (i)$. Suppose $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \mbox{ connected to } y) > 0$ for all $x,y \in U$, for some set $U\subset [0,1]^2$ with $\lambda(U) > 0$. Fix $y\in U$. By Fubini's theorem \begin{eqnarray*} \ensuremath{\mathbb{E}} \lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) &=& \int_{\Omega} \int_{[0,1]^2} 1_{D^c_{\text{fat}}}(x,\omega) d\lambda(x) d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\omega) \\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^2} \int_{\Omega} 1_{D^c_{\text{fat}}}(x,\omega) d\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\omega) d\lambda(x) \\ &=& \int_{[0,1]^2} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D^c_{\text{fat}}) d\lambda(x) \\ &\geq& \int_{U\setminus \{y\}} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \mbox{ connected to } y) d\lambda(x) > 0. \end{eqnarray*} Hence $\lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) > 0$ with positive probability. Since $\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} p_n >0$ there exists an integer $n_0$ such that $p_{n} \geq p_c(N,2)$ for all $n \geq n_0$. nodes.name: Full-measure set V
nodes.statement: $(i) \Rightarrow (iii)$. Next suppose that $\lambda(D^c_{\text{fat}}) > 0$ a.s.\ given non-extinction of the fat fractal process. For points $x\in[0,1]^2$ not on the boundary of a subcube, define the event $A^x$ as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm lebesgue}. It follows from the proof of Theorem \ref{thm lebesgue} that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(A^x)=1$ for all $x\in V$, for some set $V\subset[0,1]^2$ with $\lambda(V)=1$. By \eqref{def A^x} we have for all $x\in V$ \[ \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D^c_{\text{fat}})= \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D_{\text{fat}})>0. \]
nodes.statement_short: From the proof of Theorem 1.8, $P(A^x)=1$ on a full-measure set $V$.

nodes.name: Local connection
nodes.statement: Let $x\in V$. Then \[ 0 < \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x\in D^c_{\text{fat}}) \leq \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(\mbox{diam}(C^x_{\text{fat}}) > \textstyle{\frac{1}{n}}), \] where $\mbox{diam}(C^x_{\text{fat}})$ denotes the diameter of the set $C^x_{\text{fat}}$. nodes.statement_short: Each $x\in V$ connects to a small circle around it with positive probability.

nodes.name: Strips and Gamma_x
nodes.statement: Write $x=(x_1,x_2)$ and define the following subsets of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^2$ \begin{eqnarray*} H_1 &=& \textstyle [0,1] \times [x_2-\frac{1}{4n_x},x_2], \\ H_2 &=& \textstyle [0,1] \times [x_2,x_2+\frac{1}{4n_x}], \\ V_1 &=& \textstyle [x_1-\frac{1}{4n_x},x_1] \times [0,1], \\ V_2 &=& \textstyle [x_1,x_1+\frac{1}{4n_x}] \times [0,1]. \end{eqnarray*} Note that for every $x \in [0,1]^2$ it is the case that at least one horizontal strip $H_i$ and at least one vertical strip $V_j$ is entirely contained in $[0,1]^2$. nodes.statement_short: Define strips $H_i,V_j$ and the crossing event $\Gamma_x$.

nodes.name: Positive crossing probability
nodes.statement: See Figure \ref{fig Gamma_x} for an illustration of the event $\Gamma_x$. From Theorem 2 in \cite{ChaChaDur} it follows that in the MFP model with parameter $p \geq p_c(N,2)$, the limit set $D_p$ connects the left-hand side of $[0,1]^2$ with its right-hand side with positive probability. It then follows from the RSW lemma (e.g.\ Lemma 5.1 in \cite{DekMee}) and the FKG inequality that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{p}(\Gamma_x)>0$. Let $A_{n}$ denote the event of complete retention until level $n$, i.e.\ $\omega(C(\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}}))=1$ for all $\ensuremath{\mathbf{I}} \in \ensuremath{\mathcal{J}}^{(n-1)}$. Since $\prod_{n=1}^{\infty} p_n >0$ there exists an integer $n_0$ such that $p_{n} \geq p_c(N,2)$ for all $n \geq n_0$. Hence, the probability measure $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{\text{fat}}(\cdot | A_{n_0}$) dominates $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{p_{c}(N,2)}(\cdot)$. Since $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{\text{fat}}(A_{n_0})>0$ it follows that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_{\text{fat}}(\Gamma_x) > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: RSW, FKG and domination of critical MFP after full retention give $P(\Gamma_x)>0$.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Observe that for $x,y \in V$ \begin{eqnarray*} \lefteqn{ \{ x \mbox{ connected to } y \} } \\ &\supset& \{ x \mbox{ connected to } S(x,\textstyle{\frac{1}{2n_x}}) \} \cap \Gamma_x \cap \{ y \mbox{ connected to } S(y,\textstyle{\frac{1}{2n_y}}) \} \cap \Gamma_y. \end{eqnarray*} Since all four events on the right-hand side are increasing and have positive probability, we can apply the FKG inequality to conclude that for all $x,y\in V$ we have $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}(x \mbox{ connected to } y) > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: FKG on four increasing events connects $x$ and $y$.
